firstRoundFindings: quiz.q2: The trapezium distractor's explanation incorrectly calls a side face's outline a trapezium; each side face of this square pyramid is triangular. Correct that explanation.
quiz.q3: A sphere has no base. Replace references to slices 'parallel to the base' in the solution and option 1 with slices in parallel planes.

quiz.q6: The solution's claim that the rectangular faces are not all identical is misleading: the intended regular hexagonal prism has congruent rectangular side faces, and opposite rectangular faces are parallel. Explain the base using the direction of congruent parallel cross-sections instead; revise option 3's why because identical parallel faces alone do not distinguish the bases here.
quiz.q7: The rectangle and parallelogram options overlap, so there is not exactly one correct option. Make the distractor unambiguously false and give it an accurate mistake explanation.

quiz.q8: Option 3's why overgeneralises that slices through a pyramid are triangles and that parallel prism slices never shrink. State specifically that this horizontal plane cuts a rectangle and that only sections parallel to the triangular bases are guaranteed congruent.

theory: The intro defines a prism solely by uniform cross-section, which also includes cylinders and contradicts the later cylinder exclusion. Include the booklet's polygonal end faces and rectangular sides. The steps also presume a pair of identical end faces exists, making them unusable for the cone, pyramid and sphere uniformity questions; first choose parallel slicing planes, then check shape and size, identifying prism bases where applicable.
summary: Repaired the prism definition and slicing steps, removed references to a sphere's base, and corrected the explanations in quiz.q2, quiz.q6 and quiz.q8. Made quiz.q7's parallelogram distractor explicitly exclude right angles so exactly one option is correct; all practice items, figures, values and whole items were preserved.
reviewSummary: All 24 items have correct answers, suitable methods and supported booklet question types, and every quiz has exactly one correct option with appropriate distractor explanations. The theory is consistent with the supplied booklet, no worked examples are supplied, and no removals require review.
